## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

161	   161	    /// The gradient fill (§5.2's `shape.gradient`, format version 6): a
162	   162	    /// geometry, an angle and the stops, all of it one `set_shape` patch.
163	   163	    ///
164	   164	    /// Three rules out of the schema show up here as UI, and none of them is
165	   165	    /// this file's invention:
166	   166	    ///
167	   167	    ///  - **Every write sends the WHOLE object.** The core MERGES a nested
168	   168	    ///    object into a stored one key by key (§5.2), but a stored `null` is
169	   169	    ///    not an object: `actions::merge` replaces it with what the patch
170	   170	    ///    carries, and the keys left out then come from `Gradient::default()`
171	   171	    ///    rather than from what the clip had. This section is where a
172	   172	    ///    gradient is turned ON from null, so it sends every key and is right
173	   173	    ///    in both cases. `shadow` has carried that since M3 and `obscure`
174	   174	    ///    since phase 3; `edited` below is where `gradient` joins them.
175	   175	    ///  - **The Fill rows above stay live.** A gradient takes precedence over
176	   176	    ///    `fill` and does not clear it, which is what makes this section's
177	   177	    ///    Reset — one `{gradient: null}` — an exact inverse rather than a
178	   178	    ///    shape that goes invisible. Disabling the colour underneath would
179	   179	    ///    hide the value the Reset is about to bring back, so the note says
180	   180	    ///    where the fill went instead of the panel pretending it is gone.
181	   181	    ///  - **`line` and `arrow` get the rows DISABLED, not hidden.** The field
182	   182	    ///    is stored and range-checked on every kind and read by the two area
183	   183	    ///    kinds alone — `radius`'s precedent exactly — so flipping the Kind
184	   184	    ///    popup to Line and back may not lose the ramp.
185	   185	    func gradientSection() -> InspectorSection {
186	   186	        let binding = self.binding
187	   187	        let kinds = GradientKind.allCases
188	   188	        func current() -> Gradient? { binding.shapeProps.gradient }
189	   189	        func on() -> Bool { current() != nil }
190	   190	        /// Whether this kind has an interior to fill at all.
191	   191	        func area() -> Bool { !binding.shapeProps.kind.isLinear }
192	   192	        func list() -> [GradientStop] { current()?.stops ?? [] }
193	   193	        func at(_ index: Int) -> GradientStop? {
194	   194	            let stops = list()
195	   195	            return stops.indices.contains(index) ? stops[index] : nil
196	   196	        }
197	   197	        func ops(_ next: Gradient?) -> [ReelOp] {
198	   198	            binding.ops(shape: ShapePatch(gradient: .some(next)))
199	   199	        }
200	   200	        /// The gradient with `change` applied and the other keys as they
201	   201	        /// stand. This is the "send it whole" rule above, spelled once so that
202	   202	        /// no row has to remember it.
203	   203	        func edited(_ change: (inout Gradient) -> Void) -> [ReelOp] {
204	   204	            guard var gradient = current() else { return [] }
205	   205	            change(&gradient)
206	   206	            return ops(gradient)
207	   207	        }
208	   208	        func edited(replacing index: Int, _ stop: GradientStop) -> [ReelOp] {
209	   209	            var next = list()
210	   210	            guard next.indices.contains(index) else { return [] }
211	   211	            next[index] = stop
212	   212	            return edited { $0.stops = next }
213	   213	        }
214	   214	        /// The mixed badge for one stop's field: a selection where some clip
215	   215	        /// has no gradient, or none at that index, disagrees — which the
216	   216	        /// `nil` says, the way `obscureSection`'s `mixedAt` says it.
217	   217	        func mixedAt<T: Equatable>(_ index: Int, _ read: @escaping (GradientStop) -> T) -> Bool {
218	   218	            binding.mixedShape { props -> T? in
219	   219	                guard let stops = props.gradient?.stops, stops.indices.contains(index)
220	   220	                else { return nil }
221	   221	                return read(stops[index])
222	   222	            }
223	   223	        }
224	   224	        /// The colour half way between two stops, component by component —
225	   225	        /// which is exactly what `CGGradient` does between them, in the same
226	   226	        /// sRGB space, so a handle added here sits ON the ramp rather than
227	   227	        /// beside it. A three-component colour is an opaque one (`RGBA`'s own
228	   228	        /// rule), so both are padded the same way before they are mixed.
229	   229	        func midpoint(_ a: RGBA, _ b: RGBA) -> RGBA {
230	   230	            func component(_ color: RGBA, _ index: Int) -> Double {
231	   231	                index < color.count ? color[index] : (index == 3 ? 1 : 0)
232	   232	            }
233	   233	            return (0..<4).map { (component(a, $0) + component(b, $0)) / 2 }
234	   234	        }
235	   235	        /// A stop dropped into the WIDEST gap and coloured by the ramp that
236	   236	        /// is already there, so Add changes the picture not at all: it puts a
237	   237	        /// handle where the ramp already runs, which is what Add means in
238	   238	        /// every gradient editor. The model cannot do this for you —
239	   239	        /// `GradientStop`'s own default is black at 0, because serde has to
240	   240	        /// fill a missing key without knowing which row was clicked.
241	   241	        ///
242	   242	        /// It inserts into the list as it is HELD, never into the sorted one.
243	   243	        /// The rows are drawn in held order and the core deliberately does
244	   244	        /// not police that order (`props_check.rs` argues the missing check
245	   245	        /// where it would have gone), so sorting here would make every row
246	   246	        /// jump the first time somebody pressed Add.
247	   247	        func added(_ stops: [GradientStop]) -> [GradientStop] {
248	   248	            guard stops.count >= 2 else { return Gradient.defaultStops }
249	   249	            let ramp = stops.enumerated().sorted {
250	   250	                $0.element.at == $1.element.at
251	   251	                    ? $0.offset < $1.offset : $0.element.at < $1.element.at
252	   252	            }
253	   253	            var widest = -1.0
254	   254	            var left = ramp[0]
255	   255	            var right = ramp[1]
256	   256	            for (a, b) in zip(ramp, ramp.dropFirst()) where b.element.at - a.element.at > widest {
257	   257	                widest = b.element.at - a.element.at
258	   258	                left = a
259	   259	                right = b
260	   260	            }
261	   261	            var next = stops
262	   262	            next.insert(
263	   263	                GradientStop(
264	   264	                    at: (left.element.at + right.element.at) / 2,
265	   265	                    color: midpoint(left.element.color, right.element.color)),
266	   266	                at: left.offset + 1)
267	   267	            return next
268	   268	        }
269	   269	
270	   270	        var rows: [NSView] = [
271	   271	            inspectorCheckRow(
272	   272	                "Gradient", binding, name: "Gradient", read: on,
273	   273	                ops: { value in ops(value ? Gradient() : nil) },
274	   274	                mixed: { binding.mixedShape { $0.gradient != nil } },
275	   275	                enabled: area),
276	   276	            inspectorPopupRow(
277	   277	                "Kind", binding, name: "Gradient Kind", items: kinds.map { $0.displayName },
278	   278	                read: { kinds.firstIndex(of: current()?.kind ?? .linear) ?? 0 },
279	   279	                ops: { index in
280	   280	                    guard kinds.indices.contains(index) else { return [] }
281	   281	                    return edited { $0.kind = kinds[index] }
282	   282	                },
283	   283	                mixed: { binding.mixedShape { $0.gradient?.kind } },
284	   284	                enabled: { on() && area() }),
285	   285	            // Degrees from the RIGHT, counter-clockwise, and the same eight
286	   286	            // quick picks the shadow's angle gets, because it is the same
287	   287	            // convention and the crate has only the one.
288	   288	            inspectorValueRow(
289	   289	                "Angle", binding, name: "Gradient Angle", unit: "°", decimals: 0, min: 0,
290	   290	                max: 360, quick: [0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, 315],
291	   291	                read: { current()?.angle ?? 0 },
292	   292	                ops: { v in edited { $0.angle = v } },
293	   293	                mixed: { binding.mixedShape { $0.gradient?.angle } },
294	   294	                // A radial gradient has no direction to point: the model
295	   295	                // stores the angle through the flip all the same, so coming
296	   296	                // back to Linear finds the number where it was left.
297	   297	                enabled: { on() && area() && current()?.kind == .linear }),
298	   298	        ]
299	   299	        for index in 0..<list().count {
300	   300	            let swatch = OptionSwatchControl(
301	   301	                read: { at(index)?.color.nsColor ?? .black },
302	   302	                write: { color in
303	   303	                    guard let stop = at(index),
304	   304	                        let next = changedRGBA(color, from: stop.color)
305	   305	                    else { return }
306	   306	                    binding.apply(
307	   307	                        "Gradient Stop",
308	   308	                        edited(replacing: index, GradientStop(at: stop.at, color: next)))
309	   309	                },
310	   310	                enabled: area, onEdit: {})
311	   311	            // A stop's position is 0–1 in the model and a PERCENTAGE here,
312	   312	            // for `video.opacity`'s reason: the ramp is a distance across the
313	   313	            // box, and nobody reads 0.35 of a box as a third of the way.
314	   314	            let position = OptionFieldControl(
315	   315	                width: InspectorMetrics.fieldWidth, unit: "%", decimals: 0, min: 0, max: 100,
316	   316	                quick: [0, 25, 50, 75, 100],
317	   317	                read: { (at(index)?.at ?? 0) * 100 },
318	   318	                write: { value in
319	   319	                    guard let stop = at(index) else { return }
320	   320	                    binding.apply(
321	   321	                        "Gradient Stop",
322	   322	                        edited(replacing: index, GradientStop(at: value / 100, color: stop.color)))
323	   323	                },
324	   324	                enabled: area,
325	   325	                onEdit: { binding.edited() })
326	   326	            let remove = OptionButtonControl(
327	   327	                title: "Remove",
328	   328	                action: {
329	   329	                    var next = list()
330	   330	                    guard next.count > 2, next.indices.contains(index) else {
331	   331	                        NSSound.beep()
332	   332	                        return
333	   333	                    }
334	   334	                    next.remove(at: index)
335	   335	                    binding.apply("Remove Stop", edited { $0.stops = next })
336	   336	                },
337	   337	                enabled: { area() && list().count > 2 }, onEdit: {})
338	   338	            remove.toolTip =
339	   339	                "Take this colour off the ramp — two stops is the floor, because one "
340	   340	                + "colour is a fill and Fill above already spells that"
341	   341	            rows.append(
342	   342	                inspectorRow(
343	   343	                    "Stop \(index + 1)", [swatch, position, remove],
344	   344	                    mixed: { mixedAt(index) { $0.color } || mixedAt(index) { $0.at } }))
345	   345	        }
346	   346	        if !on() {
347	   347	            rows.append(inspectorRow(nil, [InspectorRowLabel("No gradient.")]))
348	   348	        }
349	   349	        let add = OptionButtonControl(
350	   350	            title: "Add Stop",
351	   351	            action: {
352	   352	                let next = added(list())
353	   353	                guard next.count > list().count else {
354	   354	                    NSSound.beep()
355	   355	                    return
356	   356	                }
357	   357	                binding.apply("Add Stop", edited { $0.stops = next })
358	   358	            },
359	   359	            enabled: { area() && on() && list().count < Gradient.maxStops }, onEdit: {})
360	   360	        add.toolTip =
361	   361	            "Put a handle on the ramp where the ramp already is — the widest gap, "
362	   362	            + "at the colour that is already there"
363	   363	        rows.append(inspectorButtonRow([add, InspectorRowLabel("\(Gradient.maxStops) at most")]))
364	   364	
365	   365	        return InspectorSection(
366	   366	            id: "shape.gradient", title: "Gradient",
367	   367	            summary: {
368	   368	                guard let gradient = current() else { return "off" }
369	   369	                return "\(gradient.kind.displayName.lowercased()), \(gradient.stops.count) stops"
370	   370	            },
371	   371	            note: {
372	   372	                guard area() else {
373	   373	                    return "Fills the rectangle or ellipse; a line or arrow keeps its "
374	   374	                        + "stroke colour."
375	   375	                }
376	   376	                guard on(), binding.shapeProps.fill != nil else { return nil }
377	   377	                return "The gradient covers the Fill colour above; Reset brings it back."
378	   378	            },
379	   379	            reset: { binding.apply("Gradient", shape: ShapePatch(gradient: .some(nil))) },
380	   380	            defaultExpanded: false,
381	   381	            rows: rows)
382	   382	    }

420	     2	//! [`Stroke`] around it and the [`Gradient`] (with [`GradientKind`],
421	     3	//! [`GradientStop`] and the [`MAX_GRADIENT_STOPS`] budget on it) that fills
422	     4	//! it.
423	     5	//!
424	     6	//! Cut out of `model_props.rs` in road map 5's E2, when that file stood AT
425	     7	//! the 600-line cap owing `video.motion`, and cut HERE because
426	     8	//! `model_text.rs` is its own precedent: a whole property group moved out
427	     9	//! with the types only it names. Text and shape are the two CPU-rendered,
428	    10	//! hash-keyed sources — neither reaches the fragment stage as a sampled
429	    11	//! texture the model describes, both are drawn by
430	    12	//! `LayerRenderers`/`LayerRenderersText` into one, and both are keyed by
431	    13	//! the recipe's content hash — so taking the second after the first leaves
432	    14	//! `model_props.rs` holding what the compositor's uniform block is read
433	    15	//! from and nothing else. Nothing here is ever a shader discriminant, and
434	    16	//! that is a standing rule rather than an omission: [`GradientKind`]'s own
435	    17	//! doc says a kind may be added at the END and that nothing derives a
436	    18	//! number from the order, where [`crate::model::BlendMode`]'s order IS the
437	    19	//! discriminant.
438	    20	//!
439	    21	//! Re-exported whole by `model_props.rs`, which `model.rs` re-exports whole
440	    22	//! in turn, so `crate::model::ShapeProps` and every other path is
441	    23	//! unchanged. The FIELD that holds these values (`Clip.shape`) stays in
442	    24	//! `model.rs` with the clip's other property groups.
443	    25	//!
444	    26	//! The rules are `model.rs`'s: the field names ARE the JSON keys,
445	    27	//! declaration order IS key order, every type is `#[serde(default)]` over a
446	    28	//! hand-written [`Default`] that says what an absent key means, and nothing
447	    29	//! here carries `deny_unknown_fields`.

522	   104	/// it is 8 where [`crate::model::MAX_FILTERS`] and
523	   105	/// [`crate::model::MAX_OBSCURE`] are both 4: those two are SLOTS — the uniform block carries exactly four `(kind, amount)` pairs

177	   177	    ///    Reset — one `{gradient: null}` — an exact inverse rather than a
178	   178	    ///    shape that goes invisible. Disabling the colour underneath would
179	   179	    ///    hide the value the Reset is about to bring back, so the note says
180	   180	    ///    where the fill went instead of the panel pretending it is gone.
181	   181	    ///  - **`line` and `arrow` get the rows DISABLED, not hidden.** The field
182	   182	    ///    is stored and range-checked on every kind and read by the two area
183	   183	    ///    kinds alone — `radius`'s precedent exactly — so flipping the Kind
184	   184	    ///    popup to Line and back may not lose the ramp.
185	   185	    func gradientSection() -> InspectorSection {
186	   186	        let binding = self.binding
187	   187	        let kinds = GradientKind.allCases
188	   188	        func current() -> Gradient? { binding.shapeProps.gradient }
189	   189	        func on() -> Bool { current() != nil }
190	   190	        /// Whether this kind has an interior to fill at all.
191	   191	        func area() -> Bool { !binding.shapeProps.kind.isLinear }
192	   192	        func list() -> [GradientStop] { current()?.stops ?? [] }
193	   193	        func at(_ index: Int) -> GradientStop? {
194	   194	            let stops = list()
195	   195	            return stops.indices.contains(index) ? stops[index] : nil
196	   196	        }
197	   197	        func ops(_ next: Gradient?) -> [ReelOp] {
198	   198	            binding.ops(shape: ShapePatch(gradient: .some(next)))
199	   199	        }
200	   200	        /// The gradient with `change` applied and the other keys as they
201	   201	        /// stand. This is the "send it whole" rule above, spelled once so that
202	   202	        /// no row has to remember it.
203	   203	        func edited(_ change: (inout Gradient) -> Void) -> [ReelOp] {
204	   204	            guard var gradient = current() else { return [] }
205	   205	            change(&gradient)
206	   206	            return ops(gradient)
207	   207	        }
208	   208	        func edited(replacing index: Int, _ stop: GradientStop) -> [ReelOp] {
209	   209	            var next = list()
210	   210	            guard next.indices.contains(index) else { return [] }
211	   211	            next[index] = stop
212	   212	            return edited { $0.stops = next }
213	   213	        }
214	   214	        /// The mixed badge for one stop's field: a selection where some clip
215	   215	        /// has no gradient, or none at that index, disagrees — which the
216	   216	        /// `nil` says, the way `obscureSection`'s `mixedAt` says it.
217	   217	        func mixedAt<T: Equatable>(_ index: Int, _ read: @escaping (GradientStop) -> T) -> Bool {
218	   218	            binding.mixedShape { props -> T? in
219	   219	                guard let stops = props.gradient?.stops, stops.indices.contains(index)
220	   220	                else { return nil }

222	   222	            }
223	   223	        }
224	   224	        /// The colour half way between two stops, component by component —
225	   225	        /// which is exactly what `CGGradient` does between them, in the same
226	   226	        /// sRGB space, so a handle added here sits ON the ramp rather than
227	   227	        /// beside it. A three-component colour is an opaque one (`RGBA`'s own
228	   228	        /// rule), so both are padded the same way before they are mixed.
229	   229	        func midpoint(_ a: RGBA, _ b: RGBA) -> RGBA {
230	   230	            func component(_ color: RGBA, _ index: Int) -> Double {
231	   231	                index < color.count ? color[index] : (index == 3 ? 1 : 0)
232	   232	            }
233	   233	            return (0..<4).map { (component(a, $0) + component(b, $0)) / 2 }
234	   234	        }
235	   235	        /// A stop dropped into the WIDEST gap and coloured by the ramp that
236	   236	        /// is already there, so Add changes the picture not at all: it puts a
237	   237	        /// handle where the ramp already runs, which is what Add means in
238	   238	        /// every gradient editor. The model cannot do this for you —
239	   239	        /// `GradientStop`'s own default is black at 0, because serde has to
240	   240	        /// fill a missing key without knowing which row was clicked.
241	   241	        ///
242	   242	        /// It inserts into the list as it is HELD, never into the sorted one.
243	   243	        /// The rows are drawn in held order and the core deliberately does
244	   244	        /// not police that order (`props_check.rs` argues the missing check
245	   245	        /// where it would have gone), so sorting here would make every row
246	   246	        /// jump the first time somebody pressed Add.
247	   247	        func added(_ stops: [GradientStop]) -> [GradientStop] {
248	   248	            guard stops.count >= 2 else { return Gradient.defaultStops }
249	   249	            let ramp = stops.enumerated().sorted {
250	   250	                $0.element.at == $1.element.at
251	   251	                    ? $0.offset < $1.offset : $0.element.at < $1.element.at
252	   252	            }
253	   253	            var widest = -1.0
254	   254	            var left = ramp[0]
255	   255	            var right = ramp[1]
256	   256	            for (a, b) in zip(ramp, ramp.dropFirst()) where b.element.at - a.element.at > widest {
257	   257	                widest = b.element.at - a.element.at
258	   258	                left = a
259	   259	                right = b
260	   260	            }
261	   261	            var next = stops
262	   262	            next.insert(
263	   263	                GradientStop(
264	   264	                    at: (left.element.at + right.element.at) / 2,
265	   265	                    color: midpoint(left.element.color, right.element.color)),
266	   266	                at: left.offset + 1)

268	   268	        }

content.content:
### Line and arrow endpoints

A line or arrow shape has a round handle at each end. Drag a handle to move
that end. The scale handles and the rotation grip still work on the line's
box.

### Snapping

While you drag a clip to move it, the box snaps to:

- the canvas edges, its centre lines and its thirds
- the edges and centres of every other visible layer

Scaling, rotating and cropping do not snap (⇧ while rotating snaps the angle
to 15° steps instead). A guide line is drawn across the canvas on each axis that snapped. Press
**N** or choose **View ▸ Snapping** to turn snapping on or off. The timeline
uses the same setting. Hold ⌘ during a drag to stop snapping for that drag.

683:## Image clips
684-
685-You import an image the same way as a movie (see
686-[Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)), and it lands as a 5-second clip.
687-An image has no length of its own, so you can trim it to any duration. Image
688-clips have everything on the Picture tab, Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key
689-included, and a Color tab for grading. Remove Background works on a picture too,
690-keeping its person or its foreground subject (see
691-[Remove Background](#remove-background)).
692-
693-When the Document tab's **Fit new clips to canvas** option is on, a new clip whose picture
694-is bigger than the canvas starts at Fit scale. Otherwise it starts at 100 %,
695-its native size.
696-
697-## Backgrounds
698-
699-Backgrounds are in the Clip menu. Each command puts a clip on a **new
700-back-most track** and selects it.
701-
702-| Command | What it puts there |
703-|---|---|
704-| **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color** | A canvas-sized white rectangle named "Background", starting at 0 and as long as the timeline. White because the canvas is already black. Recolour it in the Shape tab's Fill row, or turn on Gradient for a full-canvas ramp |
705-| **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image…** | A picture you choose (the panel offers only image files), scaled to fill the canvas, as long as the timeline. The picture joins the Media tab in the same undo step, or is reused if it is already there. If it can't be read, an alert says so and nothing is added |
706-| **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** | A copy of the one selected clip, playing exactly the same frames, scaled to fill the canvas, centred, uncropped and blurred at full strength. It is muted so the sound doesn't play twice, and is named "Blurred Background". This is the usual backdrop for a screen recording or a vertical video that doesn't fill the frame |
